questions.title: Gravitational field lines & circular orbits — planet mass from r³–1/ω² graph and moon speed

parts.answer: Draw at least four straight radial field lines meeting at P, with every arrow pointing along a line towards P.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The gravitational force provides the centripetal force. It has constant magnitude and is always perpendicular to the velocity (direction of motion) of the moon, so the moon follows a circular path.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: GMm/r² = mrω², so GM = r³ω², i.e. r³ = GM × (1/ω²). The gradient of the r³ – 1/ω² graph is therefore GM, giving M = gradient/G.

questions.title: Oscillating floating block — SHM, angular frequency & damped energy loss

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Upthrust and weight.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The upthrust is now greater than the weight, so the resultant force acts upwards (towards the equilibrium position).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: A, g and ρ are all constant, so the resultant force F ∝ x. The minus sign shows that F and the displacement x are in opposite directions, which is the condition for simple harmonic motion.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: F = ma = −Agρx, so a = −(Agρ/m)x. Comparing with a = −ω²x gives ω² = Agρ/m, hence ω = √(Agρ/m).

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.answer: The oscillations are damped by viscous (drag) forces in the liquid, so the amplitude decreases and the maximum negative displacement is smaller than the maximum positive displacement.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.answer:
From Fig. 3.3, a = −ω²x, so ω² = −gradient = 2.3/0.020 = 115 s⁻².
ΔE = ½mω²(x₁² − x₂²) = ½ × 0.57 × 115 × (0.020² − 0.016²) = 4.7 × 10⁻³ J

questions.title: Magnetic flux & flux linkage in solenoids — Lenz's law & induced force

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The magnetic flux is less in the smaller solenoid: the flux density B is the same in both, but the smaller solenoid has a smaller area, so Φ = BA is smaller.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The magnetic flux linkage is greater in the smaller solenoid: flux linkage = NΦ = NBA, so smaller = 3000 × 1.6 × 10⁻³ B = 4.8B, larger = 600 × 6.4 × 10⁻³ B = 3.84B.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Lenz's law: the direction of the induced e.m.f. is such that it opposes the change (in magnetic flux linkage) that produces it.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Removing the smaller solenoid changes the magnetic flux linkage, which induces an e.m.f. in it. Since its terminals are joined, a current flows, producing a magnetic field around the smaller solenoid. The two magnetic fields interact to produce an attractive force, so a force is needed to pull the solenoid out.

questions.title: Electron diffraction — de Broglie wavelength & wave nature of electrons

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: λ = h/p (or h/mv), where h is the Planck constant and p (= mv) is the momentum of the particle; m is its mass and v its velocity.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Diffraction.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Moving electrons behave like waves (they exhibit wave properties).

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: The spacing between the atoms in the crystal is approximately equal to the wavelength of the electrons, so the electrons are diffracted.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer: The diffraction rings are closer together, so the electron wavelength has decreased (the electrons have greater momentum). A shorter wavelength requires faster electrons, so the accelerating potential difference was increased.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: Sketch an upward curve of decreasing gradient from (0, 0), passing through (0.52 s, 12 × 10¹²) and (1.2 s, 18.8 × 10¹²), tending towards 24 × 10¹².

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
N(0.30 s) = 16 × 10¹² and N(0.90 s) = 7.2 × 10¹², so (16 − 7.2) × 10¹² = 8.8 × 10¹² nuclei decay.
Energy per alpha particle = 6900 × 10³ × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 1.10 × 10⁻¹² J.

questions.title: X-rays — target heating, attenuation & image contrast

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Bone (μ = 3.0 cm⁻¹) and muscle (μ = 0.22 cm⁻¹) have very different attenuation coefficients, so very different fractions of the X-rays are absorbed (transmitted), giving good contrast. Blood (μ = 0.23 cm⁻¹) and muscle have very similar μ, so similar fractions are absorbed, giving poor contrast.

questions.title: PET scanning — tracer, annihilation, gamma photon energy & imaging

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A tracer is a substance containing radioactive nuclei that is introduced into the body and absorbed by the tissue being studied.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Annihilation is the process in which a particle interacts with its antiparticle so that their mass is converted into energy.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: An electron and a positron.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer:
Each photon carries half the energy, so 2hc/λ = E.
λ = 2hc/E = 2 × 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3.00 × 10⁸/(1.64 × 10⁻¹³) = 2.43 × 10⁻¹² m

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer: The two gamma photons travel in opposite directions and are detected by detectors arranged around the body. The different arrival times of the photons at the detectors are used to locate the point of annihilation. Processing the signals produces an image showing the concentration of the tracer in the tissue.
